name: Daniel Avery
bio: A Representative from New York; born in Groton, Conn., September 18, 1766; attended the common schools; served in the Revolutionary War, appointed ensign in the Sixth Company, Eighth Regiment of the Connecticut Militia, and served as lieutenant and captain until May 1794; moved to Aurora, N.Y., in 1795 and subsequently became the owner of a large tract of land which was farmed by tenants; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Twelfth and succeeding Congress (March 4, 1811-March 3, 1815); elected to the Fourteenth Congress to fill the vacancy caused by the resignation of Enos T. Throop (September 30, 1816-March 3, 1817); resumed the management of his estate; connected with the land office at Albany, N.Y., for twenty years; died on January 30, 1842, in Aurora, Cayuga County, N.Y.; interment in Oak Glen Cemetery, Aurora, N.Y.
